reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence - PK data showed measurable plasma concentrations of both encorafenib and binimetinib with appropriate exposure levels at therapeutic doses. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: While specific pathway biomarkers weren't reported, the combination of BRAF and MEK inhibitors has well-established mechanism of MAPK pathway inhibition in BRAF-mutant tumors. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with BMRR of 66.7% in Phase 2, which is clinically meaningful for brain metastases in melanoma. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Both dose levels showed similar response rates (60% vs 66.7%), suggesting consistent efficacy across dosing regimens in this BRAF V600-mutant population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Small sample size (n=13) and single-arm design limit statistical power, but the effect size was large enough to demonstrate clinical benefit despite these limitations.

failure_modes.evidence: Very small sample size of 13 patients limits statistical power and generalizability, though the large effect size overcame this limitation
